text:
alex: Thinking about span routing for per-customer isolation — do we shard exporters by org_id or by dataset_id? Getting pushback from SRE about cardinality. TL;DR: tradeoffs.
maria: org_id keeps routing simple but mixes product areas. dataset_id gives finer isolation and retention controls and maps to billing.
sam: if we go dataset_id, can the collector enforce per-dataset TTL/labels during ingest? cc @ingrid
ingrid: yes, collector can attach dataset metadata and downstream exporters can apply TTL. main risk is mapping table size. we need compact routing rules.
jonathan: RBAC question — who should be allowed to create datasets? infra or product teams? infra owning reduces accidental mass creation.
maria: infra owns creation API but product teams provision via service accounts. audit log + approval flow. :thumbsup:
alex: perf concern: high-cardinality datasets create hot shards. suggestion: composite shard key like hash(dataset_id) ^ low_entropy(org_id) to spread load.
sam: pseudo: ```route_key = fnv1a(dataset_id) % SHARD_COUNT  # simple```. but ok to consider other hashing for re-sharding.
ingrid: fnv1a works for speed but consider jump consistent hashing for fewer movements during scaling. also add a fallback bucket for extremely hot datasets.
telemetry-bot: :rotating_light: exporter-rotation job scheduled 02:00 UTC if SHARD_COUNT changes (automated).
jonathan: ops: we need per-tenant quotas to avoid noisy neighbors. propose token-bucket per org + soft cap per dataset. alerts when usage > 75%.
alex: agreed. also retention defaults: 90d, enterprise contracts can request custom retention and dedicated shards.
maria: Console UX: show dataset -> shard mapping, retention, current ingest QPS, and let infra trigger manual reassign with cooldown and audit trail.
sam: follow-ups: perf bench plan + telemetry surface. propose exposing: span_ingest_latency, ingest_queue_depth, drop_rate, shard_backpressure.
ingrid: i'll prototype collector config + routing plugin and a small benchmark harness by EOD. tagging @alex @maria for review.
jonathan: note for rollout: start with 1% of datasets behind dataset-based routing, measure hot-shard incidents, then ramp.
alex: thanks all — i'll open a short RFC with the composite key idea and a proposed rollback plan.
maria: thanks — add the quota numbers you used in the benchmark so product can plan. :eyes:
sam: ping if you want me to run the bench on my infra cluster.
ingrid: will share configs in the rfc. end of thread.
